edge_cases.scenario: the same deletion
edge_cases.expected: its API project is soft-deleted with the owner cleared, and its keys are revoked

edge_cases.scenario: another verified account with the listing's submission email claims it afterwards
edge_cases.expected: the claim works and creates a new API project owned by that account

edge_cases.scenario: edits the first owner made to the claimed listing
edge_cases.expected: survive the deletion and show for the second owner

edge_cases.scenario: a project made in developer settings, by contrast, when its owner is deleted
edge_cases.expected: its profile is unpublished (only legacy listings stay public)

features.title: Website restriction on keys follows the project's website

edge_cases.scenario: clearing the website while a key is restricted to it
edge_cases.expected: refused with a message; the website and the key's origins stay as they were

edge_cases.scenario: changing the website while one key is restricted and another is not
edge_cases.expected: rewrites only the restricted key's origin to the new website; the unrestricted server key is unchanged

edge_cases.scenario: clearing the website when no key is restricted
edge_cases.expected: allowed; unrestricted server keys are unaffected

edge_cases.scenario: restricting a key of a project that has no website
edge_cases.expected: refused

edge_cases.scenario: restricting a key of a project with a website
edge_cases.expected: allows only the website's origin

edge_cases.scenario: in the settings page, clear the website of a project with a restricted key
edge_cases.expected: the server's refusal is shown in the form, the form stays open with the empty website; the Playwright specs expect the refusal and a passing path once the restriction is off

checks.contains: keeps the edit form and its empty website when clearing the website is refused
clearing the website is refused while a key is restricted

features.title: Internal and private profiles never reach the public listing

edge_cases.scenario: a profile whose live API project is on the internal tier, published or not
edge_cases.expected: never in GET /api/powered-by for the public or non-staff users; staff still see it

edge_cases.scenario: a private profile (no consent) with a live API project
edge_cases.expected: not listed

edge_cases.scenario: a settings-created profile with no live API project
edge_cases.expected: hidden

edge_cases.scenario: a settings-created public profile with a live API project
edge_cases.expected: listed

edge_cases.scenario: a deleted settings-made project, even if staff mark it published
edge_cases.expected: not listed

edge_cases.scenario: a logged-in non-staff user
edge_cases.expected: sees what the public sees: published and consented rows without private fields

features.title: Auth service down: fail open on the static default limits

edge_cases.scenario: chart rendered with rate limiting on
edge_cases.expected: every rule has a static numeric limit, so with no limit metadata from the auth service the static default applies

checks.contains: every rule has a static numeric limit \(fail-open\)

edge_cases.scenario: a request with no tier metadata (what an unreachable auth service yields)
edge_cases.expected: falls into rule 4, the inverted-tier catch-all, counted per client IP rather than in one shared bucket; nothing is left unlimited

edge_cases.scenario: auth service scaled to zero on a running gateway, burst past the static limit
edge_cases.expected: 429 from the static rules and no 5xx from the gateway
edge_cases.planned_check: drill: scale the auth service to zero on a cauldron, burst past the static limit, expect 429 and no 5xx

edge_cases.scenario: a logged-out browser loads a page: the HTML, /static/ files and data scripts go through the same HTTPRoute as the API
edge_cases.expected: rules 3 and 4 (per client IP) select only the API path prefix, so pages and static assets are never counted or limited, in normal operation or during an auth outage; rules 1 and 2 are unchanged

checks.contains: rule 3 keeps its tier and per-IP selectors next to the path
rule 4 keeps its tier and per-IP selectors next to the path

features.title: An older image still writes powered_by_project.tier

edge_cases.scenario: the profile carries tier partner while its api_project is developer
edge_cases.expected: the loader reads api_project.tier_id only: the key loads as developer

edge_cases.scenario: an older image writes powered_by_project.tier
edge_cases.expected: the kept profile trigger still notifies, so the auth service reloads, and the reload ignores the value

edge_cases.scenario: new code (writer, claim, account deletion) touches a profile
edge_cases.expected: never writes the frozen tier, owner or deleted_at

edge_cases.scenario: the admin edits a profile
edge_cases.expected: does not offer the frozen tier, owner or deleted_at

edge_cases.scenario: an older loader reads a tier changed on api_project
edge_cases.expected: sees the frozen profile value (documented limit)
